skill.description: Guide for adding CloudBase Web authentication with Web SDK v3, provider readiness checks, login flows, session guards, and user management.

security_audit.summary: Static command, network, filesystem, and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, public setup links, and frontend auth examples. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. A medium semantic risk remains because the skill tells agents to automatically change CloudBase auth provider settings without an explicit confirmation requirement.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before calling manageAppAuth or enabling SMS, email, anonymous, OAuth, or username password providers.
Prefer packaged references or marketplace dependency metadata over ../ sibling paths to reduce scanner noise and installation ambiguity.

remediation.issue: Public fallback URLs embedded in the skill text
remediation.suggestion: Document that remote references are read-only setup material and should not receive project secrets or user data.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Auth Provider Changes Need Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly instructs agents to automatically use auth-tool-cloudbase or manageAppAuth to enable login providers, including SMS, email, anonymous, and OAuth. Changing authentication provider settings can expand access paths if done without explicit project owner approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction pattern is explicit and repeated, but it is related to legitimate auth setup. The risk is configuration change without user confirmation, not malicious code execution.

content.value_statement: Web teams need reliable CloudBase auth flows without stale SDK patterns. This skill guides provider checks, session guards, and Web SDK v3 integration.
actual_capabilities: Guides CloudBase Web SDK v3 initialization with environment, region, and publishable key inputs.
Explains phone OTP, email OTP, password, OAuth, anonymous, custom ticket, and ID token login flows.
Shows how to verify provider readiness before adding browser sign-in or registration code.
Provides session guard guidance using getSession instead of deprecated login-state checks.
Covers user profile updates, identity linking, sign-out, token use, and account deletion patterns.
limitations: Does not configure Mini Program, native app, or server-side authentication flows.
Requires CloudBase provider setup and publishable key details from another tool or console.
Example code must be adapted to the target framework, routing system, and form structure.
Provider enablement and console changes may need explicit project owner approval.

use_cases.title: Add login to a Web app
use_cases.description: Implement CloudBase login forms with OTP, password, or OAuth while following SDK v3 auth method guidance.

use_cases.title: Protect routes with real sessions
use_cases.description: Replace unreliable login-state checks with session-based route guards that reject anonymous or missing sessions.

use_cases.title: Review auth provider readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether email, phone, username, anonymous, or OAuth providers are enabled before implementation begins.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic login page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-web-cloudbase to add a CloudBase Web login page. Check provider readiness first, then wire the existing form handlers.

prompt_templates.title: Add session-based route guards
prompt_templates.scenario: Reliable access control for protected pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-web-cloudbase to protect these routes with getSession checks. Reject missing sessions and anonymous sessions before rendering private views.

prompt_templates.title: Support multiple login methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-web-cloudbase to implement phone OTP, username password login, and OAuth. Confirm each provider before writing browser code.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and modernize CloudBase auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-web-cloudbase to review this app for deprecated auth methods, incorrect provider assumptions, and weak route guards. Propose focused fixes.

output_examples.input: Add username and password login to an existing React CloudBase app.
output: The response identifies username password as the provider to verify first.
It updates the login form to use text identifiers instead of email-only inputs.
It wires sign-in handling and reports errors without exposing secrets.

output_examples.input: Protect the dashboard after users sign in with CloudBase.
output: The response checks the current session before showing private content.
It redirects missing or anonymous sessions to the login page.
It avoids deprecated login-state helpers that can produce misleading results.

output_examples.input: Add phone OTP registration and login.
output: The response verifies phone login readiness before implementation.
It separates sending the code from verifying the received token.
It connects the SDK calls to the existing buttons and status messages.

best_practices: Verify the target auth provider before writing sign-in or sign-up code.
Use getSession for route guards and reject anonymous sessions when private access is required.
Keep secret keys out of browser code and use only publishable keys in Web clients.
anti_patterns: Do not treat deprecated login-state helpers as proof that a user is authenticated.
Do not switch username-based forms to email-only flows unless the product requires email addresses.
Do not enable new auth providers without confirming the project owner wants that change.

faq.question: Does this skill create backend authentication services?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on CloudBase Web frontend integration after provider setup is available or checked.

faq.question: Which SDK style does it target?
faq.answer: It targets CloudBase Web SDK v3 with Supabase-like auth method names and response patterns.

faq.question: Can it support username and password login?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides username password login when that provider is enabled and the account identifier is not an email address.

faq.question: Why does it prefer getSession for guards?
faq.answer: getSession can show when no real login exists. Deprecated login-state helpers may look valid with only a publishable key.

faq.question: Does it handle OAuth callbacks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains automatic callback handling and manual verification when automatic detection is not enabled.

faq.question: Is it safe to enable anonymous login?
faq.answer: Anonymous login should be used only for explicit, limited cases. Private routes should reject anonymous sessions.
